name: Facet
text: Ship EXCAVA with a one-time theme picker at first launch, defaulting to dark mode. This keeps the interface consistent with the competitive analysis while giving users control over their preference. The trade-off is a slight delay at first launch, but it avoids forcing a system-based default that might not match user expectations.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A one-time picker still forces a decision users may not care about—most won’t change it later, so the friction at launch is pure loss. Better: default to system preference, then let users toggle anytime in settings; no survey at first launch, no hidden lock-in. Settle it with a quick usability test: measure how many users change the theme within a week of first use.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Defaulting to system preference risks alienating users who never change their OS theme—dark mode isn’t universal, and forcing them to hunt for a toggle in settings buries the setting where they’ll never find it. Better: default to dark mode (as competitive analysis shows it’s expected), but expose the toggle in the top-level UI—no menus, no friction. Settle it with a 5-user hallway test: if anyone can’t find the toggle in 5 seconds, the design fails.
